entries.title: Cloud Engineer / DevOps Specialist
entries.text: I build and run GKE platforms for SaaS clients: modular Terraform, Autopilot clusters, shared or dedicated Cloud SQL, packaged as Helm charts and delivered with ArgoCD. I took clusters from Kubernetes v1.24 to v1.30 and from Ingress to Gateway API without service disruption, moved VM workloads to containers on GKE and AKS, and run CI/CD on GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Azure DevOps. I also use AI agents to produce discovery documents, technical designs and cost estimates.

featured.title: GitOps lab in one command
featured.text: One command brings up a complete GitOps environment on kind or GKE: GitLab CE as the Git server, ArgoCD with the app-of-apps pattern, and Kargo promoting releases from dev to staging to prod. A 10-step guided demo walks through it, and a guided teardown cleans up. On GKE the control plane is reachable only through its DNS endpoint with IAM.

featured.title: bekky: encrypted backups for a whole workstation
featured.text: Backs up and restores my OS configuration to Google Cloud Storage. AES-256 with PBKDF2 at 600k iterations, deduplication before encryption, secrets in a separate archive, and a manifest that re-clones every repo on restore. Nearline storage with lifecycle rules keeps the bill small. Cross-distro, scheduled with alerts, tested with bats.

featured.title: opencode mission control: live view of agent sessions
featured.text: A real-time local dashboard for opencode v2 sessions. See which agents are working, which tool is running right now, what failed and what it cost. Stall alerts flag runs that never start a session or go silent. It reads the local opencode database and has zero npm dependencies.

caseFiles.title: Case files
caseFiles.lede: Four problems on Google Cloud, with the constraints and the decision for each. Clients are not named.

items.title: Upgrading Kubernetes 1.24 to 1.30
items.context: Clusters still on Kubernetes v1.24, on-prem and in the cloud, already out of upstream support.
items.constraint: Production traffic could not stop. Every step had to be planned and rehearsed first.
items.decision: One minor version at a time, control plane first, then nodes rolled one at a time so pods always have somewhere to go.
items.result: The clusters run v1.30 with no service disruption.

items.title: Shared storage on GKE without NFS
items.context: SaaS workloads on GKE shared files over NFS: one more server to patch, size and back up.
items.constraint: No service disruption for the tenants.
items.decision: Replaced NFS with GCS Fuse, provisioned with Terraform and mounted through the Helm chart.
items.result: No NFS server left to patch, size or back up for this workload.

items.title: Releases promoted by ArgoCD Image Updater
items.context: Each new image needed a manual edit of the manifests before it reached production.
items.constraint: Every change had to go through Git, so the state of each environment stays reviewable.
items.decision: ArgoCD Image Updater detects new images and updates the target environment from Git, with no manual edit in the release path.
items.result: New builds reach live environments without a manual step, and Git shows what runs where.

items.title: Automated cloud cost estimates
items.context: Cloud cost estimates were slow to build by hand and risky to share with clients.
items.constraint: Every figure must be traceable, and internal details must never reach the client file.
items.decision: An AI-agent skill reads official list prices from the provider billing API and generates formula-based workbooks from a data model. Client and internal views are separate.
items.result: Each estimate is recomputed, scanned for confidential terms and reviewed by an independent agent before it reaches the client.
